boundary_condition: Apply only to lodging selection; do not infer this preference for flights, restaurants, car rentals, destinations, or other travel tasks.
condition: When booking lodging for a family-oriented stay or when child/family suitability is relevant to the hotel choice.
default_action: Prioritize or filter for hotels described as family-friendly or suitable for families/children.
exception_condition: If the user explicitly asks for adults-only, romantic, no-children, nightlife-focused, or otherwise non-family-oriented lodging, do not apply the family-friendly default.
name: Prioritizes hotels suitable for families and children
rationale: Three independent hotel-task sources each add family-friendly suitability as a hotel requirement. This supports a controlled synthetic-user default for family-suitable lodging, without treating the separate Taskmaster speakers as one real longitudinal user.

source_evidence.contribution: User states “Family friendly would be good,” supporting family-suitable lodging as a desired hotel feature.
User says to “make sure it's family-friendly,” again grounding the hotel feature preference.
User asks for “Family-friendly?” as a hotel requirement, matching the same reusable lodging feature.

source_examples.user_utterance: Yeah. I guess just make sure it's family-friendly, and then that's everything.
